_meta: The p-values from an A/A test: the SAME system was compared against itself on 20 different metrics, so there is no true difference on any of them -- every 'significant' result is a false positive by construction. Under the null hypothesis a p-value is uniform on [0,1], so these 20 values are 20 uniform draws (seed 7), representing 20 independent metric comparisons where nothing really changed. The trap: testing each at the usual 0.05 threshold, the chance that AT LEAST ONE clears 0.05 by luck is 1-(0.95)^20 = 0.64, so a false 'winner' is more likely than not. alpha is the per-test significance level. The p-values and alpha are the fixture; the family-wise error rate, the Bonferroni threshold, and which metrics each method flags are computed.
